key_insight: MM-Lifelong is a 181.1-hour multimodal dataset organized into Day / Week / Month scales that exposes how current multimodal lifelong systems fail on realistic, sparsely distributed daily-life footage, and the paper proposes an agentic baseline to better handle long-range, temporally heterogeneous understanding.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between hour-scale video benchmarks made of dense clips and real unscripted daily-life streams, enabling evaluation and development of models that must remember, summarize, and reason across varying temporal densities.
method: Curate MM-Lifelong: 181.1 hours of multimodal footage structured into Day / Week / Month temporal densities to reflect natural daily-life event distributions.

Benchmark existing approaches and identify two main failure modes in current paradigms (degradation of end-to-end MLLMs over long-range contexts; retrieval/memory methods struggling with sparse, variable-density events).
Introduce an agentic baseline that combines episodic summarization, targeted retrieval, and modular reasoning to mitigate forgetting and scaling issues in lifelong multimodal understanding.
impact: Provides a realistic, temporally-structured benchmark that reveals weaknesses of today’s multimodal models and supplies an agentic baseline for future work — accelerating research on memory, long-range reasoning, and deployment of agents that monitor or assist in real-world settings.

paper_title: Towards Multimodal Lifelong Understanding: A Dataset and Agentic Baseline
paper_authors: Guo Chen, Lidong Lu, Yicheng Liu, Liangrui Dong, Lidong Zou
